findings.title: The steel and granite give-way speeds (5.6 km/s, 13 km/s) and the granite page's 'no crater' rest on the shaking model's 1 ms pulse floor, not on the stop the README describes
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js PASSENGER.landGround (T = Math.max(1e-3, L / v), ~4327); README decision 4 and Known limits; Their powers card (src/static-data.js); test/powers.js section 7 (r2(vb('steel')) === 5600, r2(vb('granite')) === 13000, !lgOf(all9,'granite').gives); test/shots.js very-fast impact on granite
findings.evidence: README decision 4 says the ground's pulse is 'the person's own stop, about their size over the landing speed'. landGround instead uses T = max(1 ms, L/v). The 1 ms floor is landShake's, from the Walk tab's ground-wave model (commit 3f550ef), not a stop time. L = 0.5594 m, so the floor applies above L/1 ms = 559 m/s. The slab, asphalt, ice and soil thresholds (102, 144, 19.8-50.8 m/s) are below that and unaffected, but steel and granite are above it. My script gives bear = 5.025e8 N (steel) and 1.139e9 N (granite). landGround's vBear is 5,567 and 12,619 m/s. With the README's stop (T = L/v, mean push m v²/L) the thresholds are sqrt(bear L/m) = 1,765 m/s (steel) and 2,657 m/s (granite). At its vBear the floored stop moves the person v T/2 = 2.8 m (steel) and 6.3 m (granite) into the ground: 5 to 11 times their own size, so the ground has given way. Page, {action:'throw', obj:'person', logKg:9.15, surface:'granite'}, all-out: 'They land at 10.1 km/s ... Impact: 1.1 t TNT, all of it taken back by Safe passenger, so no crater or blast where they land.' Over the stop in their own size the mean push is 90.26 × 10,110² / 0.5594 = 1.65e10 N, 14.5 times what granite bears over 0.67 m². Even the engine's own floored Hann pulse peaks at 2 × 9.13e8 = 1.83e9 N, past the 1.14e9 N bearing.
findings.expected: With the stop decision 4 states, a person landing on granite gives the ground way from about 2.7 km/s, and on the steel deck from about 1.8 km/s. A 10.1 km/s landing on granite pushes about 15 times past what granite bears, so the page shouldn't say 'no crater'.
findings.fix: In landGround, compare the bearing with the push over the stop decision 4 describes, T = L / v, with no 1 ms floor (keep the floor in landShake, where it belongs to the shaking model): push = vToMomentum(v, m) · v / L, vBear = sqrt(bear · L / m). Update the README (decision 4, Known limits) and the Their powers card to about 1.8 km/s on steel and 2.7 km/s on granite. In powers.js expect 1,800 and 2,700 m/s. Move the shots.js granite case to a landing below 2.7 km/s (for example a 10^7.5 kg dial, which lands at 1.5 km/s), or expect the give-way sentence at 10^9.15 kg.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced, and the defect holds. PASSENGER.landGround (engine.js 4324-4331) takes T = max(1 ms, L/v). L is 0.5594 m, so the floor applies above 559 m/s. README decision 4 describes the pulse as 'the person's own stop, about their size over the landing speed' and never mentions the floor. The floor comes from landShake (added in 3f550ef with no stated reason) and belongs to the shaking model, not to a stop. Below 559 m/s the floor changes nothing (sand to ice, 19.8-144 m/s). On steel and granite it sets the thresholds the README, the Their powers card and powers.js give (5.6 and 13 km/s). With the stop the README describes, those thresholds are 1.76 and 2.66 km/s. The floored stop also contradicts itself. Stopping in 1 ms at the floored threshold speed takes v·T/2 = 2.8 m (steel) or 6.3 m (granite) of travel. That is 5 to 11 times the person's size, so the ground must already have given way. The round 1 record does say the push was chosen to equal landShake's mean push, but that choice is wrong physics, and the README describes the stop differently. On the page, a person landing on granite at 10.1 km/s gets 'no crater or blast where they land'. Over their own stop the mean push there is 14.5 times what granite bears. Even the floored Hann peak, 1.83e9 N, is past granite's bearing of 1.14e9 N. Granite's bearing is 1.7 GPa over 0.67 m², and the push over L/v is 24.6 GPa, far past any dynamic strength of rock. So 'no crater' is wrong on any reading. Minor: it affects only very fast landings on steel or granite.

findings.title: landGround compares the whole landing momentum with a vertical bearing capacity, so a grazing landing is said to make 'the ground give way' when its downward push is a small fraction of what the ground bears
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js PASSENGER.landGround (~4320); src/app.html landGivesText (Throw), the Catch miss callout (givesM) and the hits-ground text; test/shots.js round 1 block (cLogD 2, logKg 8, air 0: expects the give-way sentence at 155 m/s)
findings.evidence: landGround takes push = |p| / T and ignores the landing angle. The engine's own rule for landings, weakGround, splits the momentum. It compares the downward part J·sinθ with the bearing, and the sideways part with friction ('Sideways his landing goes in whole, as on real ground (he skids it out: nothing breaks for it)', engine.js ~2024). My script, over landShake's own T = L/v on the concrete slab: (1) Throw tab, {action:'throw', obj:'person', logKg:5.5, angle:0}, all-out. The page says 'They land at 151 m/s ... But past a landing of about 100 m/s, that push is more than the concrete slab bears ... so the ground gives way where they land'. The flight tops out at 2.74 m and lands at 2.8°, so the downward speed is 7.3 m/s, like a 2.7 m fall, and the downward mean push is 0.11 of the slab's 1.67 MN. At 0° and 10^6 or 10^7 kg it is 0.19 and 0.39. At 10° and 10^5.5 kg it is 0.40. (2) Catch miss: the shots.js case {catch, person, hard, cMiss, cLogD:2, logKg:8, airAbsorb:0} says the ground gives way at 155 m/s. I rebuilt its flight with flyTo (vE 2,690 m/s, aim 0.006°, h0 2.74 m, real air), which gives 154.74 m/s, matching the page, at an impact angle of 2.06°. The downward part is 5.56 m/s, and the downward push is 0.083 of the bearing. The default-dial fastball misses land at 5-6°, and every fastball miss is near level. (3) At the default 45° the downward part is 0.71 of the total, so by the weakGround split the slab threshold is 102/sqrt(0.707) = 121 m/s, not 'about 100 m/s'.
findings.expected: For a shallow landing the ground bears the downward part; the sideways part is a skid that, by the engine's own precedent, breaks nothing. A person skimming in at 2-3° at 150 m/s presses down with about a tenth of what the slab bears, so 'the ground gives way where they land' is wrong there.
findings.fix: Pass the landing angle to landGround and compare J·sin(θ)/T with the bearing, as weakGround does. On Throw use r.flight.impactAngleDeg. In the Catch, record impactAngleDeg in out.miss (fm.impactAngleDeg) and use the chord's angle for hits-ground. State that the README and card speeds are for a landing straight down (about 120 m/s at 45° on the slab). Update the shots.js catch case, whose 2° landing should no longer give way. The landing's shaking also treats the whole momentum as a vertical pulse, which overstates it for shallow landings; that is older than this pull request but now sets the person throw's ceiling, so mention it in Known limits.

findings.title: Below 100% absorbed, a person held whole who hits the ground is still counted with the full blast, crater and quake, though almost all of that energy is their own landing, which Safe passenger covers
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/app.html spHitsGround (requires !(hitsGround.airK > 0)), the hits-ground verdict, the blast block and duoFacts; README decision 7
findings.evidence: Page, {duoOpen:true, duoAction:'catch', cObj:'person', cStyle:'hard', cMiss:true, logKg:16, cLogD:4.5, saveV:3}, all-out. At airAbsorb 1: 'That is their landing, and Safe passenger covers it: it takes back all of that energy, so no blast ...'. The same at airAbsorb 0.999 (Things keep their form on): '... the air it meets turns to plasma around it, from the 0% of the drag that still acts, and their power keeps it whole ... The person hits the ground about 1.15 km from Rex, carrying 32.7 PJ (7.8 Mt TNT), the heat of the air it swept up on the way included, and blasts a crater up to 181 m across ..., felt like a magnitude 5.1 quake.' Safe passenger isn't mentioned. Engine (catchLeg, the same settings): hitsGround.E = 3.266e16 J and airHeat (the swept air's heat) = 3.37e14 J at 99.9%, so the person's own share is 99.0%. At 99% it is 90.6%, and at 90% it is 49%. Decision 7 justifies the exception as 'Below 100% the air it meets turns to plasma and rides with it into the ground'. That is true of only 1% of the energy at 99.9%, so the page jumps from no blast at 100% to a 7.8 Mt crater at 99.9%.
findings.expected: With Things keep their form on (kept: the person comes through whole) and Safe passenger on, the person's own landing energy, E minus the swept air's heat, is their landing and is taken back, as decision 7 says for 100%. Only the plasma's share (airHeat) is a real blast, crater or quake.
findings.fix: In spHitsGround, also accept airK > 0 when hitsGround.kept. Take back E − airHeat as the person's landing, and count only airHeat in the blast block, the crater and quake text, and duoFacts' Eair. Keep the old reading only where the person isn't kept (Things keep their form off: 'Its plasma and debris hit'). Say so in README decision 7 and the Game of catch card.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. spHitsGround (app.html 4319) requires !(airK > 0), so at 99.9% absorbed, with Things keep their form on, the person comes through whole ('their power keeps it whole'). The page still counts the full 32.7 PJ as a 181 m crater and a magnitude 5.1 quake, and doesn't mention Safe passenger. At 100% the same throw has no blast and a person who comes down unharmed. Decision 7 is stated, but its reason ('the air it meets turns to plasma and rides with it into the ground') covers only the plasma's share. In the engine that share is airHeat, 1.0% of E at 99.9%. That leaves an unjustified jump between 100% and 99.9%. It also contradicts the Throw tab's rule: throwBlast sets a passenger's landing blast to 0 at any air share below 1% of light speed and counts only the drag's own air. And it goes against the ruling that Safe passenger covers where the person lands. One correction to the reviewer's numbers: E − airHeat still includes the motion of the swept air that rides with the person (x = 0.0104 at 99.9%). The person's own energy at the hit, (γ(v_lump) − 1)mc² with v_lump = v/(1 + x/γ) (fireballAt's vLumpAt), is 97.9% at 99.9%, 82% at 99% and 24% at 90%. The reviewer had 99.0%, 90.6% and 49%. The conclusion is the same. Minor: an extreme-dial edge case, but a wrong count of the blast, crater and quake as harm.

findings.title: At unlimited strength or the top of the dial, the no-air hits-ground text says an unbounded (or 1.1 × 10²⁶ kg·m/s) push into the Earth merely 'shakes it'
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/app.html, the hits-ground verdict for spHitsGround ('Its push (...) still reaches the ground and shakes it.') and duoFacts' harm; README decision 7
findings.evidence: Page, {duoOpen:true, duoAction:'catch', cObj:'person', cStyle:'hard', cMiss:true, inf:true, cLogD:4.5}, all-out: '... carrying unbounded energy. That is their landing, and Safe passenger covers it: it takes back all of that energy, so no blast, and spreads the stop through them, so they come down unharmed. Its push (unbounded) still reaches the ground and shakes it. But past a landing of about 100 m/s ... the ground gives way where they land (the lab doesn't size the hole).' Pull request 2's page said 'carrying unbounded energy: planet-scale, so crater scaling no longer applies.' At logKg 34 the page gives 'Its push (110 septillion kg·m/s) still reaches the ground and shakes it.' Decision 4 keeps that momentum real and whole. Delivered to the whole Earth, 1.1e26 kg·m/s gives it 1.1e26 / 5.97e24 = 18 m/s and at least p²/(2 M_E) = 1.0e27 J of motion, about 2,500 times the Chicxulub impact (about 4 × 10²³ J). None of that is the person's energy that Safe passenger takes back. Any part of the ground smaller than the whole planet would get far more. An unbounded push can't be taken by the planet at all. The effort box lists only the hand's sound barrier.
findings.expected: With the momentum real and whole, a push this large isn't a local shake: at the top of the dial it moves the whole planet and carries a planet-scale energy, and an unbounded push has no physical answer. The page should say so, not 'shakes it'. Alternatively the owners could rule that the excess is 'the ground's share it can't bear' (canon's momentum case; Q9 covers a push with no push time at unlimited strength). That would be a new reading for the owners to confirm.
findings.fix: In the spHitsGround text, give the Earth's recoil p / M_E and the least energy that momentum carries into it, p²/(2 M_E), and call it planet-scale once that passes the page's planet-scale line. When p is unbounded, say the push is unbounded, so no ground or planet can take it and the lab can't model it. Count it as planet-scale harm in duoFacts. Or put the ruling question in STATUS.md under Waiting on, and say on the page which reading it uses.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. At unlimited strength the hits-ground text for a person says 'Its push (unbounded) still reaches the ground and shakes it.' At the top of the dial (logKg 34, the dial's maximum: app.html 710, num(1, 34)) it says 'Its push (110 septillion kg·m/s) still reaches the ground and shakes it.' Decision 4 keeps that momentum real and whole. Taken by the whole Earth, 1.09e26 kg·m/s gives it 18.2 m/s and at least p²/(2 M_E) = 9.9e26 J. That is about 2,000 times the canon's dinosaur-killer 5e23 J. It isn't the person's energy, so Safe passenger can't take it back, and any part of the ground smaller than the planet would get far more. An unbounded push has no physical answer, like the ruling's collision with a body held without limit. Pull request 2's page said 'unbounded energy: planet-scale, so crater scaling no longer applies'. Round 1's spHitsGround text replaced that with 'shakes it'. No decision covers extreme or unbounded momentum, and the all-out effort box lists only the hand's sound barrier. The text is harmless at moderate dials: at logKg 16 the Earth's recoil is 4e-16 m/s. It matters from about logKg 31 up (at logKg 32: 0.18 m/s and 1e23 J). Minor: extreme dial settings, but a wrong claim.
